newsitem.title: USA: US stocks face more profit-taking, durables ahead.
newsitem.headline: US stocks face more profit-taking, durables ahead.

text.p: Profit-taking is expected to continue to weigh on U.S. stocks on Friday but monthly durable goods orders data is expected to dictate the early pace.
Durable goods tend not to draw the kind of attention on a month-to-month basis that reports such as unemployment do because durables can show wild fluctuations.
However, in a week that offered economists little in the way of new data, the durable orders have taken center stage.
"I find these numbers to be very quirky," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities.
"But when you haven't had anything else all week, people start to get starved for these numbers," he added.

Economists expect September durable goods orders to rise 2.0 percent against a 3.2 percent drop in August. Excluding defense, the numbers are forecast to rise 1.3 percent versus a 3.6 percent fall in the prior month.
Absent a shock from the report, analysts generally expect a continuation of stocks' recent retreat.
"We should see more caution and a little more profit-taking," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
"The market is working its way through October jitters and now faces some November election jitters," he added.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei-225 fell 264 points to 20,740 as investor sentiment remained bogged down by uncertainties over a new coalition government.
U.S. shares were weaker in London as caution ahead of the durable goods orders held stocks in check. In London, the FTSE-100 gained seven points to 4006.
The dollar was higher in Japan, clearing 113 yen, and firmed in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries eased in early trade. The 30-year bond fell 4/32 to yield 6.86 percent.
The December S&P 500 index was unchanged at 703.75.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column explores fears on Wall Street about the possibility of a sweep by Democrats in the November general elections.
The New York Times Marketplace column writes that Tele-Communications Inc is striving to ease investor worries about the company's outlook in light of a competitive business environment.
